gloss: hire; wage, hire-fee; reward; hired man
summary: The verb is to hire: to engage a man, an army or a craftsman for a price (Gen 30:16; 2Ch 25:6; Isa 46:6). שָׂכָר is what is paid for the work or service, a hired man’s wage, a nurse’s pay, the hire of a beast, a ship’s fare (Gen 30:32; Exo 2:9; 22:14; Jon 1:3), and so the reward God gives for work done for him: “I am your shield, your reward very great” (Gen 15:1), “his reward is with him” when Yahweh comes (Isa 40:10; 62:11). שָׂכִיר is the hired man, whose wage the law says must be paid the same day (Lev 19:13; Deu 24:14–15). Phoenician and Ugaritic škr, “hire”, have the same sense.

words.summary: What is given in return for work or service: first a man’s pay, then the reward Yahweh gives for what is done for him. Its parallel is פְּעֻלָּה, “work, the wage of work” (Isa 40:10; Jer 31:16).

senses.gloss: wage, pay for work or service
senses.definition: What an employer gives a worker, servant or soldier for his work: agreed beforehand, owed when the work is done, and to be paid on the day.

evidence.note: Jacob names his pay for keeping Laban’s flocks: every speckled and spotted one “shall be my שָׂכָר”.
Laban: “Name your שָׂכָר to me, and I will give it.”
“The speckled shall be your שָׂכָר”, and then “the streaked shall be your שָׂכָר”: the wage Laban kept changing.
Pharaoh’s daughter to Moses’ mother: “nurse him for me, and I will give your שָׂכָר”.
“In his day you shall give his שָׂכָר, and the sun shall not go down on it, for he is poor and lifts up his soul to it.”
The released Hebrew slave has served six years, “double the שְׂכַר of a hired man”.
Solomon to Hiram: “the שְׂכַר of your servants I will give you, according to all you say”.
The tithe is the Levites’ “שָׂכָר … in return for (חֵלֶף) your service in the tent of meeting”: the wage is what is given in exchange for service.
Before the house was founded “there was no שְׂכַר for man, nor שְׂכַר for beast”.
The shepherd: “if it is good in your eyes, give me my שָׂכָר … and they weighed out my שָׂכָר, thirty of silver”.
“Two are better than one, for they have a good שָׂכָר for their toil.”
Nebuchadnezzar served a great service against Tyre, “yet he had no שָׂכָר, nor his army, from Tyre for the service”.
So Yahweh gives him Egypt: “it shall be the שָׂכָר for his army”.

senses.definition: The price paid for the use of something not one’s own: the hire of a borrowed animal, a passage on a ship.

evidence.note: If the owner was with the borrowed animal, the borrower does not repay; “if it was hired (שָׂכִיר), it came for its שָׂכָר”: the hire covers the loss.
Jonah found a ship going to Tarshish, “and he gave its שָׂכָר and went down into it”: the fare.

senses.definition: What Yahweh gives in return for faithfulness or work done for him, spoken of as a wage: the same word, because he repays as an honest master pays.

evidence.note: “Do not fear, Abram; I am a shield to you; your שָׂכָר is very great.” Abram had just refused the king of Sodom’s goods (Gen 14:22–23).
“Behold, the Lord Yahweh comes with strength … behold, his שָׂכָר is with him, and his פְּעֻלָּה before him.”
“Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Behold, your salvation comes; behold, his שָׂכָר is with him.’”
To Rachel weeping for her children: “there is שָׂכָר for your work … they shall return from the land of the enemy.”
Azariah to Asa: “Be strong … for there is שָׂכָר for your work.”
“Sons are the inheritance of Yahweh; the fruit of the womb is a שָׂכָר.”
Leah: “God has given me my שָׂכָר, because I gave my maid to my husband”; she names the son Issachar.
“The living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing, and they have no more שָׂכָר, for their memory is forgotten.”

evidence.locator: Gen.15.1, Deu.15.18, Deu.24.15, Isa.40.10, Isa.62.11, Ecc.9.5: שָׂכָר → μισθός; μισθός renders it ×21

evidence.note: “Behold, I come quickly, and my μισθός is with me, to give to each as his work shall be”: Isa 40:10 and 62:11 in Christ’s mouth.
“The time of the dead to be judged, and to give the μισθός to your servants the prophets.”
“The μισθός of the labourers who mowed your fields, kept back by you, cries out”: the wage of Deu 24:15 that cries to Yahweh.
“The labourer is worthy of his μισθός.”
“Call the labourers and pay them the μισθός.”
“Your μισθός is great in heaven.”
“Each will receive his own μισθός according to his own labour.”

parallels.note: “Work” and the wage it earns, set beside שָׂכָר.

evidence.note: פְּעֻלַּת שָׂכִיר, the hired man’s wage, must not stay with you till morning.

phrases.gloss: there is a reward for your work
behold, his reward is with him
the wage of a hired man

words.summary: To engage someone for a price: a man for a night, a priest, soldiers, a goldsmith, masons, counsellors, a prophet to curse. Ezra 4:5 spells it with ס. The corpus analyses its forms under the root key סכר.

senses.definition: To get the service of a person for payment named in the text: silver, a gift, mandrakes.

evidence.note: Leah to Jacob: “You must come in to me, for שָׂכֹר שְׂכַרְתִּיךָ, I have surely hired you, with my son’s mandrakes.”
With seventy pieces of silver from Baal-berith’s house Abimelech “hired worthless and reckless men”.
The Levite: “Micah has done thus to me; he has hired me, and I have become his priest”, for ten pieces of silver a year (Jdg 17:10).
Amaziah “hired a hundred thousand mighty men of valour from Israel for a hundred talents of silver”.
The Ammonites hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob and Zobah.
A thousand talents of silver “to hire for themselves chariots and horsemen”.
The Arameans thought “the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites”.
Moab “hired against you Balaam son of Beor … to curse you”.
The same, “but our God turned the curse into a blessing”.
They weigh out silver in the balance, “they hire a goldsmith, and he makes it a god”.
The money of the chest went to those “hiring masons and carpenters to restore the house of Yahweh”.
One who hires a fool and one who hires passers-by.
The adversaries were “hiring (סֹכְרִים) counsellors against them to frustrate their purpose”: spelled with ס.
Shemaiah’s prophecy was false, “Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him … he was hired (שָׂכוּר) that I should be afraid”.

senses.definition: To give one’s work for hire, of those reduced to working for food.

evidence.note: Hannah: “The full have hired themselves out (נִשְׂכָּרוּ) for bread, and the hungry have ceased”: the full and the hungry change places.

senses.definition: To work for and receive a wage.

evidence.note: “He who earns wages (הַמִּשְׂתַּכֵּר) earns wages into a bag with holes”: the reward of work drains away while Yahweh’s house lies waste.

evidence.locator: Jdg.9.4, שָׂכַר → ἐμισθώσατο; μισθόω renders the verb about ten times

evidence.note: A householder went out early “to hire (μισθώσασθαι) labourers into his vineyard”.

words.summary: Hired, and as a noun the hired man, a free worker paid by the day or the year. The law sets him beside the sojourner and apart from the slave and the household, and guards his wage.

evidence.note: A borrowed beast: “if it was שָׂכִיר, it came for its hire”.
“The Lord will shave with a razor that is hired (הַשְּׂכִירָה) beyond the River, with the king of Assyria”: Assyria, whom Ahaz paid to come against his enemies (2Ki 16:7–8), is the razor.

senses.definition: A man working for another for wages, free, not a slave, and not of the household: his wage is owed by the day, and his days are counted.

evidence.note: “The wage of a שָׂכִיר shall not stay with you all night until the morning.”
“You shall not oppress a שָׂכִיר who is poor and needy, of your brothers or of your sojourners.”
A brother who sells himself to you: “you shall not make him serve the service of a slave; as a שָׂכִיר, as a sojourner he shall be with you”.
“As a שָׂכִיר year by year he shall be with him; he shall not rule over him with harshness.”
The sabbath year’s growth is food for the household and for the שָׂכִיר and sojourner.
“A sojourner and a שָׂכִיר shall not eat of” the Passover: outside the household that the bought slave, circumcised, belongs to (Exo 12:44).
Nor of the holy things: “a sojourner of the priest, or a שָׂכִיר”.
Yahweh a swift witness “against those who oppress the שְׂכַר שָׂכִיר, the widow and the orphan”.
“Are not his days like the days of a שָׂכִיר? As a slave pants for shade, and as a שָׂכִיר waits for his wage (פָּעֳלוֹ).”
“Look away from him … till he fulfils, as a שָׂכִיר, his day.”

senses.gloss: as the years of a hireling: exactly counted
senses.definition: A hired man’s term is reckoned to the day, neither more nor less; so a time Yahweh fixes for judgment.

evidence.note: “Within three years, as the years of a שָׂכִיר, the glory of Moab shall be brought low.”
“Within a year, as the years of a שָׂכִיר, all the glory of Kedar shall fail.”
Egypt’s “hired men in her midst are like fatted calves; they too have turned and fled”.

evidence.locator: Lev.25.40, שָׂכִיר → μισθωτός; renders it about eleven times

evidence.note: “The μισθωτός, who is not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees … because he is a μισθωτός and does not care for the sheep.”
James and John left their father in the boat with the μισθωτῶν.
The son returning: “make me as one of your μισθίων”: the place Lev 25:40 gives a poor brother, as a hired man and not a son.

parallels.note: The sojourner, the other free outsider living with a household.
The slave, beside the hired man as another who waits on a master.

opposites.note: A brother who sells himself is to serve as a שָׂכִיר, not with “the service of a slave”.

phrases.gloss: as the years of a hireling

senses.definition: The pay agreed for service; once of the full wage Yahweh gives.

evidence.note: Laban: “Because you are my brother, should you serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your מַשְׂכֹּרֶת be?”
“Your father has cheated me and changed my מַשְׂכֹּרֶת ten times.”
Boaz to Ruth: “Yahweh repay your work (פָּעֳלֵךְ), and may your מַשְׂכֹּרֶת be full from Yahweh the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”

words.summary: A rarer form beside שָׂכָר, twice. In Proverbs it is plainly a wage; in Isaiah 19:10 the phrase עֹשֵׂי שֶׂכֶר may be “wage-workers”, or, if the word is a byform of סֶכֶר “dam” (the root סכר, “stop up”), “makers of dams”: the verse does not settle which.

senses.definition: What a man earns by what he does.

evidence.note: “The wicked earns a deceptive wage (פְּעֻלַּת שָׁקֶר), but he who sows righteousness a שֶׂכֶר of truth.”

senses.definition: In Egypt’s ruin, those who “make שֶׂכֶר” are grieved in soul: either labourers working for hire or men who build weirs and dams on the Nile, beside the fishermen and flax-workers of Isa 19:8–9.

evidence.note: כָּל־עֹשֵׂי שֶׂכֶר אַגְמֵי־נָפֶשׁ: “all who make שֶׂכֶר, grieved of soul”.

cognates.note: King Kilamuwa of Samʾal “hired against him the king of Assyria”, as the Hebrew kings hire Arameans and Hittites; in Neo-Punic, the gods are asked to “reward” benefactors, the same two senses as שָׂכָר.

evidence.note: “v. qal 1. HIRE, KAI 24.7/8 (Ph) … wškr ʾnk ʿly mlk ʾšr, ‘so I hired against him the king of Assyria’ … 2. REWARD, KAI 160.1 (NPu)”.

cognates.note: Ugaritic š answers to Hebrew שׂ here as in other roots. Another Ugaritic škr, “drunkenness”, belongs with Hebrew שֵׁכָר of שׁכר, not with this root.

cognates.gloss: thank, be grateful for a benefit; (of God) requite, reward
cognates.note: Arabic š is the regular match of Hebrew שׂ. Lane’s sources define شُكْر as acknowledging a benefit, including “requiting the benefit according to its desert”, and of God “the requiting” of a man; الشَّكُور, of God, is “he who gives large reward for small works”. That is close to שָׂכָר as Yahweh’s reward, but the Arabic is thanks, not hire, so the tie is argued, not shown.

evidence.note: “شُكْرٌ on the part of God signifies The requiting and commending [a person]”; الشَّكُورُ “He who gives large reward for small, or few, works”.

doctrine.statement: The dead “know nothing, and they have no more שָׂכָר” (Ecc 9:5): the reward is not received at death. Isaiah ties it to Yahweh’s coming: “behold, the Lord Yahweh comes … his שָׂכָר is with him” (Isa 40:10), “behold, your salvation comes; his שָׂכָר is with him” (Isa 62:11). Jesus takes the words as his own: “Behold, I come quickly, and my μισθός is with me, to give to each as his work shall be” (Rev 22:12); the elders sing of “the time of the dead to be judged, and to give the μισθός to your servants the prophets” (Rev 11:18); and the one who helps the poor “will be repaid at the resurrection of the just” (Luk 14:14). From the verses: the wage God has promised is given when Christ returns and the dead are raised and judged, not before; until then they have none.

The law makes the hired man’s wage a matter between the employer and Yahweh: it must not stay overnight (Lev 19:13); “in his day you shall give his שָׂכָר … lest he cry against you to Yahweh, and it be sin in you” (Deu 24:14–15). Malachi puts those who oppress the hired man’s wage beside sorcerers and adulterers as those Yahweh will witness against when he comes to judgment (Mal 3:5), and James says the wage kept back from the mowers “cries out, and the cries have entered the ears of the Lord of armies” (Jas 5:4), at “the coming of the Lord” (Jas 5:7–8). From the verses: withholding pay that is owed is not a private debt but a sin God hears and will judge.

In Zechariah the shepherd who fed the flock asks his wage: “give me my שָׂכָר … and they weighed out my שָׂכָר, thirty of silver”, and Yahweh calls it in irony “the goodly price that I was priced at by them”, to be thrown to the potter in Yahweh’s house (Zec 11:12–13). The chief priests weighed out to Judas thirty pieces of silver for Jesus (Mat 26:15); the silver, thrown down in the temple, bought the potter’s field, and Matthew says this fulfilled the prophet’s word (Mat 27:3–10). From the verses: the leaders of the people valued Yahweh’s shepherd at a slave’s price (Exo 21:32), and that shepherd was Jesus.

note: The database keys the root שׂכר (BDB u.bk.*). The verb’s tokens are also filed under BDB o.bh.aa סָכַר “hire” (the spelling of Ezr 4:5), with the same occurrences, and the corpus morphology analyses every one of them under root סכר, so the verb carries "root": "סכר" for its uses to be counted (24, of which three, Deu 24:15 and Isa 40:10; 62:11, are the noun שְׂכָרוֹ sharing the spelling); this entry names only u.bk.aa. The verb is spelled with שׂ everywhere but Ezr 4:5; it is not the root סכר “stop up”. Left out, as not of this root: שְׂלָו “quail” (u.bk.ah), which BDB files next to this root but whose cognates (Syriac salway, Arabic salwā) point to its own root שׂלו; the names שַׂלְמוֹן/שַׂלְמָא Salmon/Salma (u.bk.ak, u.bk.ai) and שַׂלְמַי Shalmai (u.bk.al; also u.bo.ae, v.dy.aj), filed here only by BDB’s order, which belong with שַׂלְמָה/שִׂמְלָה “garment”. The name שָׂכָר Sachar (u.bk.ad; 1Ch 11:35; 26:4) has no name entry yet; BDB’s key also covers seven common-noun tokens (Num 18:31 etc.), so it is not named here. Issachar is names/issachar. Leads not followed: Fisher (p. 194) sets a Ge'ez passive participle “hired” beside Ugaritic škr, but the OCR is unreadable; check the scan and Leslau/Dillmann for Ge'ez śakara. No Aramaic or Syriac cognate found: Jewish Aramaic and Syriac hire with ʾgr; the Peshitta’s ܫܟܪ “make hideous” is another root. Akkadian has no škr “hire” in the Oracc glossaries (iškāru “work assignment” is not this root).
